subject: Chemistry
title: NCERT Example 6.3: Monochloro Structural Isomers of 2-Methylbutane
summary: Free radical monochlorination of (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃ (2-methylbutane) gives 4 monochloro structural isomers, not 5: the two CH₃ groups on the CH carbon are equivalent, so the molecule has only 4 kinds of hydrogen. Replacing one H of each kind gives 1-chloro-3-methylbutane, 2-chloro-3-methylbutane, 2-chloro-2-methylbutane and 1-chloro-2-methylbutane. Counting stereoisomers (JEE), the total is 6.

notes.title: Ex 6.3 – Monochloro Structural Isomers
notes.blurb: the method, the four kinds of H, all four isomers, the stereoisomer twist and practice

keyPoints: **Number of monochloro structural isomers = number of different kinds of H.**
2-methylbutane, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃: the two CH₃ on the CH carbon are **equivalent** (one type).
4 kinds of H: the two left CH₃ (6 H), CH (1 H), CH₂ (2 H), the end CH₃ (3 H).
JEE twist: two products are chiral, so with stereoisomers the total is **6**.

blocks.p: Identify all the possible **monochloro structural isomers** expected to be formed on free radical monochlorination of **(CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃** (2-methylbutane). (NCERT Example 6.3)

Monochlorination replaces **one H by one Cl**. Equivalent H atoms give the same product, so the number of isomers equals the number of **different kinds of hydrogen**. The trap is counting carbons: five carbons do **not** mean five isomers, because the two CH₃ groups on the CH carbon are equivalent.

blocks.p: 1-chloro-2-methylbutane and 2-chloro-3-methylbutane each have a **chiral carbon**, so each exists as a pair of enantiomers. Counting stereoisomers, the total is **4 + 2 = 6** (asked in JEE Main 2024).
